name: La Reine Marlene - SIA Project 23 24
description:
La Reine Marlene is a company specialized in the sale of home materials
    and products. The company is redesigning its information system in order
    to improve operational efficiency and customer service.

    The system supports interactions with a large network of suppliers.
    Suppliers must register in the system by providing credentials and company
    information, including VAT number, address, and an IBAN for payments.
    Registered suppliers can submit proposals for their products by specifying
    the product category, selling price to La Reine Marlene, availability,
    photos, description, and guaranteed delivery time.

    After a product proposal has been submitted, the supplier cannot modify it
    until a response is received. The administration department is notified
    whenever a new proposal is submitted and evaluates it by choosing among
    three possible outcomes: accepted, revisions requested, or rejected.

    If a proposal is accepted, a separate order-management process starts and
    the retail price to be displayed in the store is added to the order
    information. If revisions are requested, the administration department
    must explain them in a comment. The supplier is notified and has five
    working days to modify the proposal, add response comments, and resubmit it.
    If the supplier does not modify the proposal within the deadline, the
    proposal is removed from the system and the supplier is notified.

    Administrators receive a reminder every 48 hours for proposals that are
    still waiting to be evaluated. If a proposal is not evaluated within ten
    working days, the system automatically rejects it and notifies the supplier.

    Once ordered products are shipped and arrive at one of the La Reine Marlene
    stores, the goods-receiving staff verifies each product. Since the company
    does not use warehouses, every available product is directly exposed in the
    store. Products are catalogued according to category, available quantity,
    and store location.

    During goods reception, the operator checks each delivered product. If no
    problem is found, the product is confirmed and the system proposes a list
    of possible store locations. The operator selects a location and the product
    is passed to the staff responsible for placing it in the store and printing
    the corresponding price. If a problem is detected, the operator reports it
    by adding a comment and the product is not admitted into the store.

    At the end of the receiving procedure, the order department processes the
    result. If all products have been accepted, the order is completed and the
    supplier is paid. Otherwise, the order is updated and remains open while
    waiting for a later delivery that completes it. In both cases, specific
    notifications are sent to the supplier.

    The system tracks inventory levels in real time. When a product reaches a
    predefined critical reorder threshold, the order department receives an
    automatic notification. Administrators can configure automatic reorder and
    replenishment actions for selected products.

    In case of automatic reordering, an order is sent to a predefined supplier,
    who has two working days to confirm it. If no critical threshold and
    automatic reorder rule are defined, the order department manages the new
    order through a separate process.

    Customers can purchase products either in physical stores or through the
    online store. Registered online customers can browse the digital catalogue,
    select products and quantities, and complete an order. The system
    automatically calculates the order total, including taxes and shipping costs.

    Customers can pay using Visa or Mastercard credit cards, PayPal, Satispay,
    the La Reine Marlene purchase card, or an immediate online bank transfer
    through supported banks.

    Once an online order has been paid, the system tracks the delivery in real
    time. Customers receive a link by email that allows them to follow the
    shipment status. Customers who have provided consent to use their mobile
    phone number also receive notifications when estimated delivery times are
    updated. Once the product is delivered, the order is marked as completed.

    Deliveries are performed by partner shipping companies. Each online purchase
    is randomly assigned to a shipping provider. The same online shopping
    procedures are available both through the website and through the dedicated
    application.

    The information system also provides customer support. Customers can submit
    questions, assistance requests, and complaints by opening support tickets.
    Each support ticket is automatically assigned to a customer-service agent.
    The agent is notified and has 24 hours to respond. If no response is provided
    within that time, the ticket is reassigned to another operator and service
    statistics are updated.

    When the customer receives a response, the customer is notified and has five
    working days to reply. If no reply is received within that period, the ticket
    is automatically considered closed.

    Finally, the system collects data regarding orders, sales, inventory, and
    customer support. These data are used by company management to analyze
    business performance and support strategic decision making.

highLevelGoals: The supplier aims to successfully register their company information, including VAT number, address, and IBAN, to become an authorized partner of La Reine Marlene.
The supplier seeks to efficiently submit detailed product proposals, including category, selling price, availability, photos, description, and guaranteed delivery time.
The supplier desires to receive timely notifications regarding the evaluation status of their product proposals (accepted, revisions requested, or rejected).
The supplier needs the ability to modify and resubmit proposals within a specified timeframe when revisions are requested by the administration department.
The supplier expects to receive notifications and payments for products that have been accepted and processed through the order management system.
The administrator aims to efficiently review and evaluate all submitted product proposals from suppliers.
The administrator needs to clearly communicate the outcome of proposal evaluations (accepted, revisions requested with comments, or rejected) to suppliers.
The administrator seeks to be reminded of pending proposals and ensure all proposals are evaluated within the defined timeframe to prevent automatic rejection.
The administrator desires to configure and manage automatic reorder and replenishment actions for selected products based on critical reorder thresholds.
The goods-receiving operator aims to accurately verify each delivered product against order details upon arrival at the store.
The goods-receiving operator needs to efficiently report any problems or discrepancies detected with delivered products, preventing them from being admitted into the store.
The goods-receiving operator seeks to select and assign appropriate store locations for accepted products to be displayed.
The store staff aims to efficiently place newly received products in their designated store locations and print corresponding price labels.
The order department staff aims to process the results of the goods reception procedure to update and finalize orders, ensuring accurate inventory and supplier payments.
The order department staff needs to manage new orders, including those triggered by critical reorder thresholds or through a separate manual process.
The order department staff expects to receive automatic notifications when a product's inventory level reaches a predefined critical reorder threshold.
The customer aims to easily browse the digital catalogue, select desired products and quantities, and add them to an order.
The customer seeks to complete purchases securely, either in physical stores or through the online store, using various payment methods.
The customer desires to track the real-time status of their online orders and deliveries, receiving updates via email or mobile notifications.
The customer needs to be able to submit questions, assistance requests, or complaints by opening support tickets and respond to agent replies.
The customer-service agent aims to efficiently receive, manage, and respond to customer support tickets, assistance requests, and complaints.
The customer-service agent seeks to provide responses to customer tickets within a 24-hour timeframe, ensuring prompt customer service.
Company management aims to access and utilize collected data regarding orders, sales, inventory, and customer support for business analysis.
Company management seeks to leverage business performance data to inform and support strategic decision-making processes for the company.

The system allows the operator to log issues such as damaged items, incorrect quantities, or wrong products for a received delivery.
The system allows the operator to attach additional information, such as textual notes or images, to a reported product delivery problem.
The system allows the operator to flag a specific delivered product as unacceptable for admission into the store due to a detected issue.
The system provides a list or map of available physical locations within the store where products can be placed.
The system allows the operator to link a received and accepted product to a designated physical location within the store.
The system allows the operator to adjust the stock level of a product for a particular store location after placement.
The system provides the store staff with a list of products that have been received and are awaiting placement on the store floor.
The system allows the store staff to mark a product as physically placed in its assigned location within the store.
The system allows the store staff to initiate the generation and printing of price labels for selected products.
The system allows the order department staff to access reports detailing the outcome of product deliveries and verification.
The system allows the order department staff to modify the status of a purchase order (e.g., 'partially received', 'fully received') according to the goods reception report.
The system allows the order department staff to approve payment to a supplier once the corresponding products have been successfully received and verified.
The system allows the order department staff to manually initiate and create a new order for products.

The system allows the order department staff to confirm and proceed with an automatically suggested reorder.

The system allows the customer to delete a selected product from their virtual shopping cart.
The system allows the customer to change the number of units for a product already present in their shopping cart.
The system allows the customer to choose from available payment options (e.g., credit card, digital wallet) during online checkout.

The system sends a notification or displays a message to the customer confirming that their online order and payment were successful.
The system allows the customer to begin the payment process for a purchase made in a physical store.
The system allows the customer to query and view the real-time progress of their online order's delivery.
The system automatically sends email alerts to the customer when their online order's status changes (e.g., 'shipped', 'out for delivery').
The system automatically sends mobile alerts (e.g., SMS, push notification) to the customer when their online order's status changes.
The system allows the customer to initiate a new request for assistance, question, or complaint.
The system allows the customer to access a list of all their submitted support tickets, along with their current status and past interactions.

The system allows the agent to claim ownership of an unassigned support ticket for resolution.
The system allows the agent to access all information related to a selected support ticket, including customer query and history.
The system allows the agent to change the resolution status of a support ticket (e.g., 'in progress', 'resolved', 'closed').
The system allows the agent to compose and send a message in response to a customer's support ticket.
The system automatically notifies the agent when a support ticket is approaching its service level agreement (SLA) deadline for a response.
The system allows management to generate and view reports detailing sales performance over a chosen timeframe.
The system allows management to generate and view reports on current stock levels, categorized by product or product type.
The system allows management to access key performance indicators related to customer support, such as resolution time and ticket volume.
The system provides a visual dashboard displaying critical metrics related to orders, sales, inventory, and customer support.
The system allows management to create tailored reports by selecting and combining different data points from orders, sales, inventory, and customer support.
The system allows management to download collected business data in a format compatible with external analytical software.

branch_002.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Suppliers to Create and Submit Comprehensive Product Proposals
branch_002.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the entire workflow for a supplier to define, detail, and submit a product proposal. They cover the initiation of the proposal, the specification of various product attributes (category, description, images), commercial terms (price, availability, delivery timeframe), and the final act of submission. All these operations are integral steps in the process of a supplier making a new product offering for evaluation.

branch_003.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Supplier to Monitor Product Proposal Evaluation
branch_003.rationale: The low-level goals collectively ensure that suppliers are kept informed about the progress and outcome of their product proposals. This includes providing mechanisms for suppliers to actively query the evaluation status and automatically notifying them of critical updates such as acceptance, rejection, or requests for revisions.

branch_004.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Enable suppliers to revise and resubmit proposals' is fully supported by the project description, which states that if revisions are requested, the supplier has five working days to modify the proposal, add response comments, and resubmit it. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Supplier to Revise and Resubmit Product Proposals' captures the same functional intention. The goal is distinct from 'Allow suppliers to submit product proposals' (initial submission) and 'Provide suppliers with proposal status updates' (receiving notifications). It accurately reflects the supplier's need to act on feedback within a specific timeframe. Therefore, it should be kept. The parent HLG 'Enable suppliers to revise and resubmit proposals' requires the supplier to modify and resubmit proposals when revisions are requested. The documentation states: 'The supplier is notified and has five working days to modify the proposal, add response comments, and resubmit it.' The current LLGs cover: 1) retrieving details and comments (llg_001), which is necessary to know what to modify; 2) modifying the existing proposal (llg_002); and 3) resubmitting the revised proposal (llg_003). These LLGs collectively cover the essential capabilities required by the parent HLG. The documentation explicitly mentions 'add response comments' as part of the modification process. While llg_002 says 'edit the content', it is reasonable to interpret this as including the addition of response comments, or at least the core modification action. However, looking closely, 'add response comments' is a specific action distinct from just editing product fields. Is it essential? The text says 'modify the proposal, add response comments, and resubmit it'. The LLGs do not explicitly mention adding response comments. But 'modify the proposal' is a broad term. In requirements engineering, if a specific sub-action like 'add response comments' is explicitly listed in the documentation alongside 'modify', it might be considered a distinct capability. However, often 'modify' encompasses updating any editable field, including a comments field. Given the instruction to be conservative and not regenerate for minor granularity issues unless an essential capability is absent, and considering that 'modify the proposal' is the primary action, the current LLGs are sufficient. The notification of the deadline is handled by the sibling HLG 'Provide suppliers with proposal status updates' or the system's automatic rejection logic, not necessarily a supplier action to 'check deadline'. The supplier's action is to act within the deadline. The LLGs cover the actions. Therefore, KEEP_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS is appropriate.

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
La Reine Marlene is a company specialized in the sale of home materials
    and products. The company is redesigning its information system in order
    to improve operational efficiency and customer service.

    The system supports interactions with a large network of suppliers.
    Suppliers must register in the system by providing credentials and company
    information, including VAT number, address, and an IBAN for payments.
    Registered suppliers can submit proposals for their products by specifying
    the product category, selling price to La Reine Marlene, availability,
    photos, description, and guaranteed delivery time.

    After a product proposal has been submitted, the supplier cannot modify it
    until a response is received. The administration department is notified
    whenever a new proposal is submitted and evaluates it by choosing among
    three possible outcomes: accepted, revisions requested, or rejected.

    If a proposal is accepted, a separate order-management process starts and
    the retail price to be displayed in the store is added to the order
    information. If revisions are requested, the administration department
    must explain them in a comment. The supplier is notified and has five
    working days to modify the proposal, add response comments, and resubmit it.
    If the supplier does not modify the proposal within the deadline, the
    proposal is removed from the system and the supplier is notified.

    Administrators receive a reminder every 48 hours for proposals that are
    still waiting to be evaluated. If a proposal is not evaluated within ten
    working days, the system automatically rejects it and notifies the supplier.

    Once ordered products are shipped and arrive at one of the La Reine Marlene
    stores, the goods-receiving staff verifies each product. Since the company
    does not use warehouses, every available product is directly exposed in the
    store. Products are catalogued according to category, available quantity,
    and store location.

    During goods reception, the operator checks each delivered product. If no
    problem is found, the product is confirmed and the system proposes a list
    of possible store locations. The operator selects a location and the product
    is passed to the staff responsible for placing it in the store and printing
    the corresponding price. If a problem is detected, the operator reports it
    by adding a comment and the product is not admitted into the store.

    At the end of the receiving procedure, the order department processes the
    result. If all products have been accepted, the order is completed and the
    supplier is paid. Otherwise, the order is updated and remains open while
    waiting for a later delivery that completes it. In both cases, specific
    notifications are sent to the supplier.

    The system tracks inventory levels in real time. When a product reaches a
    predefined critical reorder threshold, the order department receives an
    automatic notification. Administrators can configure automatic reorder and
    replenishment actions for selected products.

    In case of automatic reordering, an order is sent to a predefined supplier,
    who has two working days to confirm it. If no critical threshold and
    automatic reorder rule are defined, the order department manages the new
    order through a separate process.

    Customers can purchase products either in physical stores or through the
    online store. Registered online customers can browse the digital catalogue,
    select products and quantities, and complete an order. The system
    automatically calculates the order total, including taxes and shipping costs.

    Customers can pay using Visa or Mastercard credit cards, PayPal, Satispay,
    the La Reine Marlene purchase card, or an immediate online bank transfer
    through supported banks.

    Once an online order has been paid, the system tracks the delivery in real
    time. Customers receive a link by email that allows them to follow the
    shipment status. Customers who have provided consent to use their mobile
    phone number also receive notifications when estimated delivery times are
    updated. Once the product is delivered, the order is marked as completed.

    Deliveries are performed by partner shipping companies. Each online purchase
    is randomly assigned to a shipping provider. The same online shopping
    procedures are available both through the website and through the dedicated
    application.

    The information system also provides customer support. Customers can submit
    questions, assistance requests, and complaints by opening support tickets.
    Each support ticket is automatically assigned to a customer-service agent.
    The agent is notified and has 24 hours to respond. If no response is provided
    within that time, the ticket is reassigned to another operator and service
    statistics are updated.

    When the customer receives a response, the customer is notified and has five
    working days to reply. If no reply is received within that period, the ticket
    is automatically considered closed.

    Finally, the system collects data regarding orders, sales, inventory, and
    customer support. These data are used by company management to analyze
    business performance and support strategic decision making.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: The project description explicitly states that the system collects data on orders, sales, inventory, and customer support, and that this data is used by company management to 'analyze business performance and support strategic decision making.' The current HLGs for Company Management ('Access comprehensive business performance data' and 'Support strategic decision-making') fully cover these documented responsibilities. No other actor-level functional goals are missing from the description; all other workflows (supplier registration/proposals, admin evaluation, goods receiving, store staff placement, order management, customer shopping/support, and agent ticket handling) are adequately represented by the existing HLGs.

branch_001.rationale: The original HLG 'Enable suppliers to register and provide company details' and the existing HLG 'Supplier Registration' both describe the exact same functional intention: the supplier registering their company and payment details (VAT, address, IBAN) to become an authorized partner. The project description supports this single workflow. Having two HLGs for the same actor covering the same semantic intent constitutes redundancy. The original HLG should be removed in favor of the existing 'Supplier Registration' HLG (or vice versa, but since we are evaluating the original against the current list which already contains 'Supplier Registration', the original is the duplicate to remove).

branch_002.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Allow suppliers to submit product proposals' is fully supported by the project description, which details the specific data points (category, price, availability, photos, etc.) suppliers must provide. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Suppliers to Create and Submit Comprehensive Product Proposals' is semantically equivalent but slightly more verbose. The original goal is concise, accurately scoped to the initial submission phase (distinct from the separate HLG for revising/resubmitting), and clearly expresses the supplier's functional intention. There is no need to rewrite it as it is not generic, ambiguous, or incorrectly scoped. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) comprehensively decompose the High-Level Goal (HLG) 'Allow suppliers to submit product proposals'. The project description explicitly lists the required data points for a proposal: product category, selling price, availability, photos, description, and guaranteed delivery time. The existing LLGs (llg_002 through llg_007) map directly to these specific attributes, while llg_001 covers the initiation of the proposal and llg_008 covers the final submission action. All capabilities are explicitly grounded in the documentation, and there are no missing essential capabilities or unsupported/misleading LLGs. The decomposition is accurate and complete.

branch_003.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Provide suppliers with proposal status updates' is fully supported by the project description, which explicitly states that suppliers are notified when revisions are requested, when a proposal is automatically rejected, and when orders are completed or updated. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Supplier to Monitor Product Proposal Status' is semantically equivalent but slightly broader (implying active querying), whereas the documentation emphasizes the system's role in sending notifications. The original goal is concise, accurately scoped to the supplier's need for information on proposal outcomes, and distinct from the goals of submitting or revising proposals. replacement_request.generation_project_description:
La Reine Marlene is a company specialized in the sale of home materials
    and products. The company is redesigning its information system in order
    to improve operational efficiency and customer service.

    The system supports interactions with a large network of suppliers.
    Suppliers must register in the system by providing credentials and company
    information, including VAT number, address, and an IBAN for payments.
    Registered suppliers can submit proposals for their products by specifying
    the product category, selling price to La Reine Marlene, availability,
    photos, description, and guaranteed delivery time.

    After a product proposal has been submitted, the supplier cannot modify it
    until a response is received. The administration department is notified
    whenever a new proposal is submitted and evaluates it by choosing among
    three possible outcomes: accepted, revisions requested, or rejected.

    If a proposal is accepted, a separate order-management process starts and
    the retail price to be displayed in the store is added to the order
    information. If revisions are requested, the administration department
    must explain them in a comment. The supplier is notified and has five
    working days to modify the proposal, add response comments, and resubmit it.
    If the supplier does not modify the proposal within the deadline, the
    proposal is removed from the system and the supplier is notified.

    Administrators receive a reminder every 48 hours for proposals that are
    still waiting to be evaluated. If a proposal is not evaluated within ten
    working days, the system automatically rejects it and notifies the supplier.

    Once ordered products are shipped and arrive at one of the La Reine Marlene
    stores, the goods-receiving staff verifies each product. Since the company
    does not use warehouses, every available product is directly exposed in the
    store. Products are catalogued according to category, available quantity,
    and store location.

    During goods reception, the operator checks each delivered product. If no
    problem is found, the product is confirmed and the system proposes a list
    of possible store locations. The operator selects a location and the product
    is passed to the staff responsible for placing it in the store and printing
    the corresponding price. If a problem is detected, the operator reports it
    by adding a comment and the product is not admitted into the store.

    At the end of the receiving procedure, the order department processes the
    result. If all products have been accepted, the order is completed and the
    supplier is paid. Otherwise, the order is updated and remains open while
    waiting for a later delivery that completes it. In both cases, specific
    notifications are sent to the supplier.

    The system tracks inventory levels in real time. When a product reaches a
    predefined critical reorder threshold, the order department receives an
    automatic notification. Administrators can configure automatic reorder and
    replenishment actions for selected products.

    In case of automatic reordering, an order is sent to a predefined supplier,
    who has two working days to confirm it. If no critical threshold and
    automatic reorder rule are defined, the order department manages the new
    order through a separate process.

    Customers can purchase products either in physical stores or through the
    online store. Registered online customers can browse the digital catalogue,
    select products and quantities, and complete an order. The system
    automatically calculates the order total, including taxes and shipping costs.

    Customers can pay using Visa or Mastercard credit cards, PayPal, Satispay,
    the La Reine Marlene purchase card, or an immediate online bank transfer
    through supported banks.

    Once an online order has been paid, the system tracks the delivery in real
    time. Customers receive a link by email that allows them to follow the
    shipment status. Customers who have provided consent to use their mobile
    phone number also receive notifications when estimated delivery times are
    updated. Once the product is delivered, the order is marked as completed.

    Deliveries are performed by partner shipping companies. Each online purchase
    is randomly assigned to a shipping provider. The same online shopping
    procedures are available both through the website and through the dedicated
    application.

    The information system also provides customer support. Customers can submit
    questions, assistance requests, and complaints by opening support tickets.
    Each support ticket is automatically assigned to a customer-service agent.
    The agent is notified and has 24 hours to respond. If no response is provided
    within that time, the ticket is reassigned to another operator and service
    statistics are updated.

    When the customer receives a response, the customer is notified and has five
    working days to reply. If no reply is received within that period, the ticket
    is automatically considered closed.

    Finally, the system collects data regarding orders, sales, inventory, and
    customer support. These data are used by company management to analyze
    business performance and support strategic decision making.

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
La Reine Marlene is a company specialized in the sale of home materials
    and products. The company is redesigning its information system in order
    to improve operational efficiency and customer service.

    The system supports interactions with a large network of suppliers.
    Suppliers must register in the system by providing credentials and company
    information, including VAT number, address, and an IBAN for payments.
    Registered suppliers can submit proposals for their products by specifying
    the product category, selling price to La Reine Marlene, availability,
    photos, description, and guaranteed delivery time.

    After a product proposal has been submitted, the supplier cannot modify it
    until a response is received. The administration department is notified
    whenever a new proposal is submitted and evaluates it by choosing among
    three possible outcomes: accepted, revisions requested, or rejected.

    If a proposal is accepted, a separate order-management process starts and
    the retail price to be displayed in the store is added to the order
    information. If revisions are requested, the administration department
    must explain them in a comment. The supplier is notified and has five
    working days to modify the proposal, add response comments, and resubmit it.
    If the supplier does not modify the proposal within the deadline, the
    proposal is removed from the system and the supplier is notified.

    Administrators receive a reminder every 48 hours for proposals that are
    still waiting to be evaluated. If a proposal is not evaluated within ten
    working days, the system automatically rejects it and notifies the supplier.

    Once ordered products are shipped and arrive at one of the La Reine Marlene
    stores, the goods-receiving staff verifies each product. Since the company
    does not use warehouses, every available product is directly exposed in the
    store. Products are catalogued according to category, available quantity,
    and store location.

    During goods reception, the operator checks each delivered product. If no
    problem is found, the product is confirmed and the system proposes a list
    of possible store locations. The operator selects a location and the product
    is passed to the staff responsible for placing it in the store and printing
    the corresponding price. If a problem is detected, the operator reports it
    by adding a comment and the product is not admitted into the store.

    At the end of the receiving procedure, the order department processes the
    result. If all products have been accepted, the order is completed and the
    supplier is paid. Otherwise, the order is updated and remains open while
    waiting for a later delivery that completes it. In both cases, specific
    notifications are sent to the supplier.

    The system tracks inventory levels in real time. When a product reaches a
    predefined critical reorder threshold, the order department receives an
    automatic notification. Administrators can configure automatic reorder and
    replenishment actions for selected products.

    In case of automatic reordering, an order is sent to a predefined supplier,
    who has two working days to confirm it. If no critical threshold and
    automatic reorder rule are defined, the order department manages the new
    order through a separate process.

    Customers can purchase products either in physical stores or through the
    online store. Registered online customers can browse the digital catalogue,
    select products and quantities, and complete an order. The system
    automatically calculates the order total, including taxes and shipping costs.

    Customers can pay using Visa or Mastercard credit cards, PayPal, Satispay,
    the La Reine Marlene purchase card, or an immediate online bank transfer
    through supported banks.

    Once an online order has been paid, the system tracks the delivery in real
    time. Customers receive a link by email that allows them to follow the
    shipment status. Customers who have provided consent to use their mobile
    phone number also receive notifications when estimated delivery times are
    updated. Once the product is delivered, the order is marked as completed.

    Deliveries are performed by partner shipping companies. Each online purchase
    is randomly assigned to a shipping provider. The same online shopping
    procedures are available both through the website and through the dedicated
    application.

    The information system also provides customer support. Customers can submit
    questions, assistance requests, and complaints by opening support tickets.
    Each support ticket is automatically assigned to a customer-service agent.
    The agent is notified and has 24 hours to respond. If no response is provided
    within that time, the ticket is reassigned to another operator and service
    statistics are updated.

    When the customer receives a response, the customer is notified and has five
    working days to reply. If no reply is received within that period, the ticket
    is automatically considered closed.

    Finally, the system collects data regarding orders, sales, inventory, and
    customer support. These data are used by company management to analyze
    business performance and support strategic decision making.

The goal 'Support strategic decision-making' is the higher-level business outcome, while 'Access comprehensive business performance data' is the functional capability that enables it. The original goal 'Access comprehensive business performance data' is a valid functional intention (accessing/viewing data) distinct from the strategic outcome. There are no other High-Level Goals for the Supplier actor that cover this specific intention (distinct from registration or revision/resubmission). There are no missing essential capabilities required by the parent HLG, and no LLGs are unsupported or misleading based on the project description. The decomposition is granular but valid for capturing the specific fields required for a proposal.

branch_004.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Enable suppliers to revise and resubmit proposals' is fully supported by the project description, which states that if revisions are requested, the supplier has five working days to modify the proposal, add response comments, and resubmit it. This represents a distinct functional intention from submitting initial proposals or registering. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Supplier to Revise and Resubmit Product Proposals' is semantically equivalent to the original, merely adding the word 'Product' for clarity. Since the original goal is supported, reasonably scoped, and not a duplicate of other supplier goals (which cover registration and initial submission), it should be kept. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) accurately decompose the High-Level Goal (HLG) 'Enable suppliers to revise and resubmit proposals'. The documentation states that when revisions are requested, the supplier is notified, has five working days to modify the proposal, add response comments, and resubmit it. The existing LLGs cover: 1) retrieving details/comments (necessary to know what to revise), 2) modifying the proposal (the core action), and 3) resubmitting the revised proposal (the final action). The capability to 'add response comments' is implicitly covered by the modification/resubmission process or can be considered part of the modification step, and no essential capability is missing. The LLGs are supported by the documentation and do not duplicate sibling HLGs (e.g., initial submission or registration).

branch_006.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Evaluate Product Proposals' accurately captures the core functional intention of the administrator to assess submitted proposals and determine their outcome (accepted, revisions requested, or rejected). This is directly supported by the project description. While the reconstructed goal 'Manage Product Proposal Evaluation and Decision-Making' is slightly broader, the original goal is sufficiently specific and faithful to the documentation. It does not overlap with other administrator HLGs like 'Communicate proposal decisions and feedback' (which focuses on the notification/communication aspect) or 'Ensure timely proposal evaluation' (which focuses on reminders and deadlines). Therefore, the original goal should be kept. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) comprehensively cover the essential capabilities required by the parent High-Level Goal 'Evaluate Product Proposals'. The workflow involves retrieving pending proposals (llg_001), viewing details to assess them (llg_002), and making one of the three documented decisions: accepting (llg_003), rejecting (llg_004), or requesting revisions with feedback (llg_005). The documentation explicitly states that the administration department evaluates proposals by choosing among these three outcomes. The sibling HLG 'Communicate proposal decisions and feedback' handles the notification aspect, which is correctly excluded from this HLG's LLGs. There are no missing essential capabilities or unsupported LLGs.

branch_007.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Communicate proposal decisions and feedback' is supported by the documentation, which states that the administration department evaluates proposals and that suppliers are notified of the outcome (accepted, revisions requested, or rejected). However, there is a significant semantic overlap with the existing HLG 'Evaluate Product Proposals'. In the context of this system, the act of evaluating a proposal inherently includes making the decision and communicating it to the supplier (e.g., adding comments for revisions, triggering notifications). The documentation describes this as a single workflow: 'evaluates it by choosing among three possible outcomes... The supplier is notified'. Splitting this into 'Evaluate' and 'Communicate' creates two HLGs that describe the same functional intention from slightly different angles (the internal decision vs. the external notification). To avoid redundancy and maintain a clear goal hierarchy, these should be merged. The 'Evaluate Product Proposals' HLG is the primary functional goal, and the communication aspect is a consequence of that evaluation. Therefore, the 'Communicate...' HLG should be removed as it is subsumed by the evaluation process.

high_level_associated.description: The administrator needs to assess submitted product proposals and decide on their outcome (accepted, revisions requested, or rejected).

actor.name: Administrator
actor.description: Evaluates product proposals, requests revisions, configures automatic reorder rules, and receives reminders for pending evaluations.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: The project description explicitly states that the system collects data on orders, sales, inventory, and customer support, and that this data is used by company management to 'analyze business performance and support strategic decision making.' The current HLG list for Company Management includes 'Access comprehensive business performance data' and 'Support strategic decision-making,' which fully cover these documented intentions. No other functional, actor-level goals for Company Management are described in the text. All other actors' responsibilities (Supplier, Administrator, Goods-Receiving Operator, Store Staff, Order Department Staff, Customer, Customer-Service Agent) are also adequately covered by the existing HLGs.

branch_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Suppliers to Create and Submit Product Proposals
branch_001.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete workflow for a supplier to define all necessary attributes and terms for a product and then submit this information as a formal proposal. Each goal represents a distinct step in the process of preparing and finalizing a product proposal, from initiation to submission for evaluation.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Supplier creates a new product proposal
Supplier adds product category to a proposal
Supplier specifies selling price for a product in a proposal
Supplier sets product availability for a proposal
Supplier uploads product photos for a proposal
Supplier provides a detailed product description for a proposal
Supplier specifies guaranteed delivery time for a product in a proposal
Supplier submits the complete product proposal for review

branch_002.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Supplier to Revise and Resubmit Product Proposals
branch_002.rationale: These low-level goals collectively describe the complete process for a supplier to receive feedback on a submitted product proposal, make necessary edits based on that feedback, and then submit the updated version for re-evaluation. They are all integral steps in managing the revision cycle of proposals.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Supplier retrieves the details and comments for a proposal requiring revisions
Supplier modifies an existing product proposal
Supplier resubmits a revised product proposal

branch_003.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage Product Proposal Evaluation and Decision-Making
branch_003.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete workflow for an administrator to review, assess, and make a final decision on product proposals. This includes retrieving a list, viewing details, and updating the status to accepted, rejected, or requesting revisions with feedback, all of which are integral steps in the evaluation and decision-making process.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Retrieve Pending Product Proposals
View Product Proposal Details
Accept Product Proposal
Reject Product Proposal
Request Revisions for Product Proposal

branch_004.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Facilitate Administrator Oversight of Proposal Deadlines
branch_004.rationale: Both low-level goals contribute to the administrator's ability to effectively monitor and manage the timelines for proposal evaluations. One provides proactive alerts for critical deadlines, while the other offers a comprehensive visual overview of all proposal statuses and deadlines.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Administrator receives reminders for pending product proposals nearing their evaluation deadline
Administrator views a dashboard showing proposals by evaluation status and remaining time

branch_005.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the capabilities an administrator needs to configure, activate, deactivate, update, and monitor the system's automatic reorder functionality for products. They all contribute to the overarching objective of controlling and overseeing this automated inventory replenishment process.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Administrator defines a critical reorder threshold for a specific product
Administrator enables automatic reorder for a product
Administrator disables automatic reorder for a product
Administrator modifies an existing reorder rule for a product
Administrator views a list of all configured automatic reorder rules

branch_006.rationale: These low-level goals collectively describe the essential steps involved in the process of receiving products into a system. They cover accessing expected delivery details, recording the actual arrival of items, and verifying that the received items match the order, all of which are critical components of a comprehensive product receiving workflow.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Goods-Receiving Operator retrieves details of an incoming delivery order
Goods-Receiving Operator scans or inputs product identifiers for received items
Goods-Receiving Operator marks a product as verified against the order

branch_007.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the process of identifying, documenting, and taking action on problems found during the reception of products. They cover logging issues, providing additional details, and making decisions about the acceptability of delivered items, all of which contribute to effectively managing discrepancies in product deliveries.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Goods-Receiving Operator reports a discrepancy for a delivered product
Goods-Receiving Operator adds notes or photos to a reported discrepancy
Goods-Receiving Operator marks a product as rejected due to a problem

branch_008.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage In-Store Product Placement and Location
branch_008.rationale: These low-level goals collectively describe the process of assigning products to specific physical locations within a store. This includes identifying available locations, linking products to those locations upon receipt, and subsequently adjusting the stock levels for products at those designated spots. The overarching intention is to maintain accurate records of where products are physically stored within the retail environment.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Goods-Receiving Operator views available store locations
Goods-Receiving Operator assigns a specific store location to an accepted product
Goods-Receiving Operator updates the inventory count for a product at a specific location

branch_009.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Prepare Received Products for Sale on the Store Floor
branch_009.rationale: These operations collectively describe the essential steps involved in transitioning newly received products from the receiving area to being fully ready and available for purchase by customers on the store floor. They cover identifying products for placement, confirming their physical placement, and ensuring they are correctly priced and labeled.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Store Staff retrieves a list of products ready for placement
Store Staff confirms placement of a product in its designated store location
Store Staff requests printing of price labels for specific products

branch_010.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the essential actions performed by the order department staff to complete the administrative and financial closure of a purchase order after products have been delivered and verified. This includes monitoring delivery outcomes, updating the order's status, and authorizing payment, all of which are steps towards finalizing the purchase order.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Order Department Staff retrieves goods reception reports
Order Department Staff updates an order status based on goods reception results
Order Department Staff authorizes payment to a supplier based on verified goods reception

branch_011.rationale: These low-level goals collectively describe the various actions an order department staff member performs to create, review, modify, and cancel purchase orders, whether initiated manually or through automated suggestions. They cover the complete lifecycle of managing product procurement.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Order Department Staff creates a new manual purchase order
Order Department Staff reviews automatically generated reorder proposals
Order Department Staff approves an automatically generated reorder
Order Department Staff modifies an existing purchase order
Order Department Staff cancels a purchase order

branch_012.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Facilitate timely identification and management of low product stock
branch_012.rationale: Both low-level goals contribute to ensuring that the order department staff is promptly informed about products with critically low stock levels. llg_001 provides an automatic alert, while llg_002 offers a continuous monitoring capability, both serving the purpose of enabling timely action to manage and replenish stock.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Order Department Staff receives an alert when a product's inventory falls below its critical reorder threshold
Order Department Staff views a dashboard of products with critical inventory levels

branch_013.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Allow Customer to Select Products for Purchase
branch_013.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete process a customer follows to identify desired products, gather necessary information about them, and then manage their selection within a virtual shopping cart. This sequence of operations is essential for preparing an order before proceeding to checkout and payment.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Customer searches for products by keyword or category
Customer views product details
Customer adds a product with a specified quantity to their shopping cart
Customer removes a product from their shopping cart
Customer updates the quantity of a product in their shopping cart

branch_014.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the necessary functionalities for a customer to successfully complete a payment for a purchase. This includes selecting payment options, securely providing payment information, initiating the payment process in various contexts (online and physical store), and receiving confirmation of a successful transaction. All these operations are integral steps in enabling and facilitating customer payments.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Customer selects a payment method for an online order
Customer submits payment details for an online order
Customer receives confirmation of a successful online purchase
Customer initiates an in-store payment transaction

branch_015.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Provide Comprehensive Order Status Information to Customers
branch_015.rationale: The low-level goals collectively aim to ensure that customers are well-informed about the status and delivery progress of their online orders. llg_001 enables customers to actively query for real-time progress, while llg_002 and llg_003 ensure they receive timely, proactive updates through various communication channels (email and mobile alerts). Together, these operations provide a complete solution for keeping customers informed throughout the order fulfillment process.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Customer retrieves the current delivery status of an online order
Customer receives email notifications for order status changes
Customer receives mobile notifications for order status changes

branch_016.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete lifecycle of a customer's interaction with a support system. They cover initiating a new request, tracking its status and history, actively participating in ongoing discussions, and receiving timely notifications about updates. All these operations are essential for a customer to effectively manage their support needs and engage with customer service.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Customer creates a new support ticket
Customer views the status and history of their support tickets
Customer adds a reply or comment to an existing support ticket
Customer receives a notification when a support agent replies to their ticket

branch_017.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Effectively Manage Customer Support Ticket Responses
branch_017.rationale: The low-level goals collectively aim to empower agents to provide timely and appropriate responses to customer support tickets. One goal provides the means to compose and send responses, while the other ensures that these responses are delivered within critical service level agreement deadlines, thereby improving overall customer satisfaction and operational efficiency.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Customer-Service Agent sends a reply to a customer support ticket
Customer-Service Agent receives alerts for tickets nearing their response time SLA

branch_018.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Management to Monitor Business Performance and Operations
branch_018.rationale: All low-level goals contribute to providing management with various reports, key performance indicators, and a consolidated dashboard to track and understand the performance of sales, inventory, orders, and customer support, thereby enabling effective oversight of business operations.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Company Management retrieves sales reports for a specified period
Company Management retrieves inventory reports by product or category
Company Management retrieves customer support ticket metrics
Company Management views a dashboard of key business performance indicators

branch_019.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable comprehensive business data analysis for management
branch_019.rationale: Both low-level goals contribute to the overarching objective of providing management with the necessary tools and data to understand business performance, identify trends, and make informed decisions, whether through internal reporting or external analytical tools.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Company Management generates custom analytical reports based on various data sets
Company Management exports business performance data for external analysis tools

The existing LLGs (llg_002 through llg_007) map directly to these specific data entry requirements. Additionally, llg_001 covers the initiation of the proposal and llg_008 covers the final submission action. There are no missing essential capabilities required by the parent HLG, and no LLGs are unsupported or misleading based on the project description. The decomposition is complete and accurate.

The original goal is well-scoped, distinct from the order department's role in managing the resulting orders, and faithful to the source text. There is no overlap with other HLGs that would necessitate removal or rewriting. branch_010.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Process goods reception results for orders' is fully supported by the project description, which states: 'At the end of the receiving procedure, the order department processes the result. If all products have been accepted, the order is completed and the supplier is paid. Otherwise, the order is updated and remains open...'. The goal accurately captures the actor's intention to finalize or update orders based on the outcome of the goods reception process. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Process Orders Following Goods Reception' is semantically equivalent but slightly less precise regarding the specific trigger (reception results). The original goal is clear, correctly scoped to the Order Department Staff, and distinct from 'Manage new orders and reorders' (which deals with initiating new orders, not finalizing existing ones based on delivery). Therefore, the original goal should be kept. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) accurately decompose the High-Level Goal (HLG) 'Process goods reception results for orders'. 
1. 'Retrieves goods reception reports' covers the input data needed to process the results.
2. 'Updates an order status' covers the core action of finalizing or keeping the order open based on the reception outcome (completed vs. partially received/open).
3. 'Authorizes payment' covers the specific consequence mentioned in the description: 'If all products have been accepted... the supplier is paid.'
4. 'Sends a notification to the supplier' covers the requirement: 'In both cases, specific notifications are sent to the supplier.'

All essential capabilities explicitly required by the project description for this specific workflow are present. There are no unsupported or misleading LLGs. The decomposition is complete and consistent with the documentation.

high_level_evaluation.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Receive notifications for critical inventory levels' is supported by the project description, which states: 'When a product reaches a predefined critical reorder threshold, the order department receives an automatic notification.' However, this goal is too narrow and passive. The actor's intention is not merely to receive a notification, but to act upon it to ensure inventory is replenished. The existing HLG 'Manage new orders and reorders' for the same actor already covers the action of managing orders triggered by these thresholds. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Manage Product Reorder Points' is also somewhat generic but closer to the operational intent. More importantly, the specific act of 'receiving notifications' is a mechanism, not the ultimate goal. The goal is to handle the critical inventory situation. Since 'Manage new orders and reorders' explicitly includes 'including those triggered by critical reorder thresholds', the specific HLG for receiving notifications is redundant and splits the intention of handling reorder triggers. The notification is the trigger for the management process. Therefore, the specific HLG for receiving notifications should be removed as it is subsumed by the broader 'Manage new orders and reorders' goal, or at least, keeping it separate creates a fragmented view of the reorder workflow. However, looking closely at the description: 'If no critical threshold and automatic reorder rule are defined, the order department manages the new order through a separate process.' This implies that when a threshold *is* reached, the notification is the key event that prompts the staff to either trigger an automatic reorder (if configured) or manually manage it. The HLG 'Manage new orders and reorders' covers the manual/automatic order creation. The HLG 'Receive notifications...' is a distinct functional requirement (the system must send it, the staff must see it). But is it a high-level goal? Usually, 'receiving a notification' is a low-level goal or a feature. The high-level goal is 'Ensure timely replenishment' or 'Manage inventory levels'. Given the existing HLG 'Manage new orders and reorders' covers the outcome, and 'Configure and manage automatic reorder rules' (Administrator) covers the setup, the Order Department Staff's specific goal is to act on the low stock. The current HLG 'Receive notifications...' is a means to an end. It is better to remove it and ensure 'Manage new orders and reorders' is robust, or rewrite it to 'Handle critical inventory alerts'. However, the prompt asks to decide between Keep, Rewrite, or Remove. 'Receive notifications' is a valid functional intention (the staff wants to be informed). But is it distinct enough from 'Manage new orders'? The description says 'the order department receives an automatic notification'. It doesn't explicitly say they 'manage' the notification itself, but they use it to manage orders. The HLG 'Manage new orders and reorders' description says 'including those triggered by critical reorder thresholds'. This suggests the notification is the trigger for that management. Therefore, having a separate HLG for just receiving the notification is redundant and splits the workflow. I will remove it to avoid fragmentation, as the core intent is managing the resulting order/reorder, which is already covered.

branch_018.rationale: The project description explicitly states: 'Finally, the system collects data regarding orders, sales, inventory, and customer support. These data are used by company management to analyze business performance and support strategic decision making.' The original High-Level Goal 'Access comprehensive business performance data' accurately captures the first part of this intention (accessing/analyzing the data). The other existing HLG for Company Management, 'Support strategic decision-making', captures the second part (using the data for decisions). While these two goals are closely related, they represent distinct functional intentions: one is about the availability and access to the data itself (the 'what'), and the other is about the application of that data for strategy (the 'why'). Keeping both allows for a clear separation between the data reporting/analytics capability and the strategic planning capability. The original goal is supported, correctly scoped to the actor, and distinct enough from the other HLG to warrant retention. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) accurately decompose the High-Level Goal (HLG) 'Access comprehensive business performance data'. The project description explicitly states that the system collects data regarding 'orders, sales, inventory, and customer support' for management analysis. The existing LLGs cover: 1) Sales reports (llg_001), 2) Inventory reports (llg_002), 3) Customer support metrics (llg_003), and 4) A consolidated dashboard (llg_004). While 'orders' is mentioned in the HLG description, order data is inherently part of sales performance and operational metrics, which are covered by the sales reports and the comprehensive dashboard. There are no unsupported LLGs, and no essential capability explicitly required by the HLG is missing. The decomposition is complete and consistent with the documentation.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: The project description outlines the responsibilities for all identified actors, and the current High-Level Goals (HLGs) comprehensively cover these intentions. Specifically: 1) Supplier goals cover registration (implied by the start of the workflow), proposal submission, and revision/resubmission. 2) Administrator goals cover proposal evaluation, timely evaluation reminders, and configuration of reorder rules. 3) Goods-Receiving Operator goals cover verification, problem reporting, and location assignment. 4) Store Staff goals cover placing products and printing prices. 5) Order Department Staff goals cover processing reception results, managing new/reorders, and receiving critical inventory notifications. 6) Customer goals cover browsing, purchasing, tracking deliveries, and managing support tickets. 7) Customer-Service Agent goals cover timely responses. 8) Company Management goals cover accessing data and supporting strategic decisions. No distinct functional actor-level intentions are missing from the current list.
